```{r setup S1, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis', cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE}
#Unique ID for each item, as well as category memberships
categorize_statement <- function(statement, categories, id_list) {
  for (category in names(categories)) {
    if (statement %in% categories[[category]]) {
      statement_index <- which(categories[[category]] == statement)
      unique_id <- id_list[[category]][statement_index]
      return(list(category = category, unique_id = unique_id))
    }
  }
  return(list(category = "Uncategorized", unique_id = NA))
}

id_list <- list()

unique_id <- 1
for (category in names(categories)) {
  num_statements <- length(categories[[category]])
  id_list[[category]] <- unique_id:(unique_id + num_statements - 1)
  unique_id <- unique_id + num_statements
}

statement_info <- mapply(categorize_statement, 
                                    final_data$statements, 
                                    MoreArgs = list(categories = categories, id_list = id_list),
                                    SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

final_data$category <- sapply(statement_info, function(x) x$category)
final_data$unique_id <- sapply(statement_info, function(x) x$unique_id)


#create independent variables and categories
final_data = final_data %>%
  mutate(category_nr = as.numeric(str_extract(category, "\\d+")),
    type = ifelse(category_nr < 13,  "Climate", "Neutral"),
    subtype = ifelse(category_nr %in% c(1,2,7,8), "Happen", ifelse(category_nr %in% c(3,4,9,10), "Anthropogenic", ifelse(category_nr %in% c(5,6,11,12), "Risk",
                  ifelse(category_nr %in% c(13,14,19,20), "Nano", ifelse(category_nr %in% c(15,16,21,22), "AI", "GMO"))))),
    strength = ifelse((type=='Climate' &  category_nr%%2==0) | (type=="Neutral" & category_nr%%2 !=0), "Strong", "Weak"),
    direction = ifelse(category_nr %in% c(1:6, 13:18), "Pro/Risky", "Contra/Nonrisky"),
    crt1 = ifelse(Q2 == 4, 1, 0),
    crt2 = ifelse(Q3 ==10, 1,0),
    crt3 = ifelse(Q4 == 39,1,0),
    crt4 = ifelse(toupper(Q5) %in% c("2", '2 PLACE', "SECOND"),1,0),
    crt5 = ifelse(Q6 == 8,1,0),
    crt6 = ifelse(toupper(Q7) %in% c("EMILY"),1,0),
    crt = rowSums(cbind(crt1,crt2,crt3,crt4,crt5,crt6),na.rm=T))



#recoding for statistical analysis
final_data = final_data %>%
  mutate(partisanship_stat = ifelse(DemRep_C == "Strongly Republican", -3, ifelse(DemRep_C == "Republican", -2, ifelse(DemRep_C== "Lean Republican", -1, ifelse(DemRep_C == "Lean Democratic", 1, ifelse(DemRep_C == "Democratic", 2,ifelse(DemRep_C == "Strongly Democratic", 3,0)))))),
         prior = ifelse(subtype == "Happen", climate1_1, ifelse(subtype == "Anthropogenic", climate2_1, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(17,19,23,48,44), climate3_3, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(18,23,47), climate3_2, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(20,21,41,42,46), climate3_1, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(24,45,43), climate3_4, NA)))))),
        nano = rowMeans(cbind(nano_1,nano_2, nano_3, nano_4), na.rm=T),
         gmo = rowMeans(cbind(gmo_1,gmo_2,gmo_3,gmo_4), na.rm=T),
         ai = rowMeans(cbind(artificial_1, artificial_2,artificial_3, artificial_4), na.rm=T),
         prior= ifelse(subtype=='Nano', nano, ifelse(subtype =='GMO', gmo, ifelse(subtype=='AI', ai, prior))),
         prior = prior -50,#to center on 0
         prior = prior/50,
         partisanship_stat = partisanship_stat/3,
         ResponseRecoded = ifelse(ResponseValue == 'Weak', 0, 1),
         ResponseTime = as.POSIXct(ResponseTime, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OSZ", tz = "UTC"),
         DifficultyResponseTime = as.POSIXct(DifficultyResponseTime, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OSZ", tz = "UTC"),
         QRT = as.numeric(difftime(DifficultyResponseTime, ResponseTime, units = "secs")),
         accuracy = ifelse(ResponseValue==strength, 1,0),
         StrengthRecoded = ifelse(strength == "Weak", -0.5,0.5),
         DirectionRecoded = ifelse (direction == "Pro/Risky", 0.5,-0.5),
         Consistency = ifelse((prior <= 0 & direction == "Contra/Nonrisky") | (prior > 0 & direction == "Pro/Risky"), "Consistent", "Inconsistent"),
         polConsistency = ifelse((partisanship_stat < 0 & direction == "Contra/Nonrisky") | (partisanship_stat > -1 & direction == "Pro/Risky"), "Consistent", "Inconsistent")) 

study1_data = final_data
```

```{r setup S2a, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis', cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE}
#Unique ID for each item, as well as category memberships
categorize_statement <- function(statement, categories, id_list) {
  for (category in names(categories)) {
    if (statement %in% categories[[category]]) {
      statement_index <- which(categories[[category]] == statement)
      unique_id <- id_list[[category]][statement_index]
      return(list(category = category, unique_id = unique_id))
    }
  }
  return(list(category = "Uncategorized", unique_id = NA))
}

id_list <- list()

unique_id <- 1
for (category in names(categories)) {
  num_statements <- length(categories[[category]])
  id_list[[category]] <- unique_id:(unique_id + num_statements - 1)
  unique_id <- unique_id + num_statements
}

statement_info <- mapply(categorize_statement, 
                                    final_data$statements, 
                                    MoreArgs = list(categories = categories, id_list = id_list),
                                    SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

final_data$category <- sapply(statement_info, function(x) x$category)
final_data$unique_id <- sapply(statement_info, function(x) x$unique_id)


#create independent variables and categories
final_data = final_data %>%
  mutate(category_nr = as.numeric(str_extract(category, "\\d+")),
    type = ifelse(category_nr < 13,  "Climate", "Neutral"),
    subtype = ifelse(category_nr %in% c(1,2,7,8), "Happen", ifelse(category_nr %in% c(3,4,9,10), "Anthropogenic", ifelse(category_nr %in% c(5,6,11,12), "Risk",
                  ifelse(category_nr %in% c(13,14,19,20), "Nano", ifelse(category_nr %in% c(15,16,21,22), "AI", "GMO"))))),
    strength = ifelse((type=='Climate' &  category_nr%%2==0) | (type=="Neutral" & category_nr%%2 !=0), "Strong", "Weak"),
    direction = ifelse(category_nr %in% c(1:6, 13:18), "Pro/Risky", "Contra/Nonrisky"))


#recoding for statistical analysis
final_data = final_data %>%
  mutate(partisanship_stat = ifelse(DemRep_C == "Strongly Republican", -3, ifelse(DemRep_C == "Republican", -2, ifelse(DemRep_C== "Lean Republican", -1, ifelse(DemRep_C == "Lean Democratic", 1, ifelse(DemRep_C == "Democratic", 2,ifelse(DemRep_C == "Strongly Democratic", 3,0)))))),
         prior = ifelse(subtype == "Happen", climate1_1, ifelse(subtype == "Anthropogenic", climate2_1, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(17,19,23,48,44), climate3_3, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(18,22,47), climate3_2, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(20,21,41,42,46), climate3_1, ifelse(unique_id %in% c(24,45,43), climate3_4, NA)))))),
         nano = rowMeans(cbind(nano_1,nano_2, nano_3, nano_4), na.rm=T),
         gmo = rowMeans(cbind(gmo_1,gmo_2,gmo_3,gmo_4), na.rm=T),
         ai = rowMeans(cbind(artificial_1, artificial_2,artificial_3, artificial_4), na.rm=T),
         prior= ifelse(subtype=='Nano', nano, ifelse(subtype =='GMO', gmo, ifelse(subtype=='AI', ai, prior))),
         prior = prior -50,#to center on 0
         prior = prior/50,
         partisanship_stat = partisanship_stat/3,
         ResponseRecoded = ifelse(ResponseValue == 'Weak', 0, 1),
         accuracy = ifelse(ResponseValue==strength, 1,0),
         StrengthRecoded = ifelse(strength == "Weak", -0.5,0.5),
         DirectionRecoded = ifelse (direction == "Pro/Risky", 0.5,-0.5),
         Consistency = ifelse((prior <= 0 & direction == "Contra/Nonrisky") | (prior > 0 & direction == "Pro/Risky"), "Consistent", "Inconsistent"),
         polConsistency = ifelse((partisanship_stat < 0 & direction == "Contra/Nonrisky") | (partisanship_stat > -1 & direction == "Pro/Risky"), "Consistent", "Inconsistent"))%>%
  filter(order < 37)

library(stringdist)

# Convert statements to a factor to ensure each statement is printed only once
final_data$statements <- as.factor(final_data$statements)

# Combine all category statements into a single vector with names to keep track of categories
all_category_statements <- unlist(categories)

# Function to find uncategorized statements using approximate matching
find_uncategorized_statements <- function(statements, category_statements) {
  uncategorized <- c()
  
  for (statement in statements) {
    # Calculate the minimum string distance to any category statement
    min_distance <- min(stringdist::stringdist(statement, category_statements))
    
    # Define a threshold for considering a statement "uncategorized" (e.g., edit distance of 5)
    if (min_distance > 5) {
      uncategorized <- c(uncategorized, statement)
    }
  }
  
  return(unique(uncategorized))
}
```

```{r setup S2b, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis', cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE}
#Unique ID for each item, as well as category memberships
categorize_statement <- function(statement, categories, id_list) {
  for (category in names(categories)) {
    if (statement %in% categories[[category]]) {
      statement_index <- which(categories[[category]] == statement)
      unique_id <- id_list[[category]][statement_index]
      return(list(category = category, unique_id = unique_id))
    }
  }
  return(list(category = "Uncategorized", unique_id = NA))
}

}

# Function to find uncategorized statements using approximate matching
find_uncategorized_statements <- function(statements, category_statements) {
  uncategorized <- c()
  
  for (statement in statements) {
    # Calculate the minimum string distance to any category statement
    min_distance <- min(stringdist::stringdist(statement, category_statements))
    
    # Define a threshold for considering a statement "uncategorized" (e.g., edit distance of 5)
    if (min_distance > 5) {
      uncategorized <- c(uncategorized, statement)
    }
  }
  
  return(unique(uncategorized))
}
```

```{r setup S3, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis', cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE}
# Load the stringdist package
if (!requireNamespace("stringdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("stringdist")
}
library(stringdist)

# More efficient categorization approach
# Create a lookup table for faster matching
create_statement_lookup <- function(categories) {
  lookup_table <- data.frame(
    statement = character(),
    category = character(),
    unique_id = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  unique_id <- 1
  for (category in names(categories)) {
    category_statements <- categories[[category]]
    # Remove NA or empty entries
    category_statements <- category_statements[!is.na(category_statements) & category_statements != ""]
    
    if (length(category_statements) > 0) {
      temp_df <- data.frame(
        statement = category_statements,
        category = category,
        unique_id = unique_id:(unique_id + length(category_statements) - 1),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      lookup_table <- rbind(lookup_table, temp_df)
      unique_id <- unique_id + length(category_statements)
    }
  }
  
  return(lookup_table)
}

# Alternative: Direct exact matching first, then fuzzy for unmatched
categorize_statements_hybrid <- function(statements, categories, threshold = 3) {
  # Create lookup table
  lookup_table <- create_statement_lookup(categories)
  
  n_statements <- length(statements)
  results <- data.frame(
    category = rep("Uncategorized", n_statements),
    unique_id = rep(NA, n_statements),
    distance = rep(Inf, n_statements),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  

  # Step 1: Try exact matches first (much faster)
  for (i in seq_along(statements)) {
    statement <- statements[i]
    if (!is.na(statement) && statement != "") {
      exact_match <- which(lookup_table$statement == statement)
      if (length(exact_match) > 0) {
        results$category[i] <- lookup_table$category[exact_match[1]]
        results$unique_id[i] <- lookup_table$unique_id[exact_match[1]]
        results$distance[i] <- 0
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Step 2: Fuzzy match for uncategorized statements
  uncategorized_indices <- which(results$category == "Uncategorized")

  if (length(uncategorized_indices) > 0) {
    for (idx in uncategorized_indices) {
      statement <- statements[idx]
      
      if (!is.na(statement) && statement != "") {
        # Calculate distances
        distances <- stringdist(statement, lookup_table$statement, method = "lv")
        min_distance <- min(distances, na.rm = TRUE)
        
        if (!is.na(min_distance) && min_distance <= threshold) {
          best_index <- which.min(distances)
          results$category[idx] <- lookup_table$category[best_index]
          results$unique_id[idx] <- lookup_table$unique_id[best_index]
          results$distance[idx] <- min_distance
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}

    # Define a threshold for considering a statement "uncategorized" (e.g., edit distance of 5)
    if (min_distance > 5) {
      uncategorized <- c(uncategorized, statement)
    }
  }
  
  return(unique(uncategorized))
}


study3_data = final_data
rm(list=setdiff(ls(), c("study3_data", "study2_data", "study2b_data", "study1_data")))
```

```{r model caching helper, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# ---- Model caching ----------------------------------------------------------
# Slow mixed-effects models are fit once, saved to disk, and reloaded on later
# knits so they don't have to be re-estimated every time the document is built.
#
# fit_or_load(model_id, <model call>)
#   * The first time it runs, it fits the model and writes it to
#     model_cache/<model_id>.rds
#   * On every subsequent run it simply reads that file back -- the model call is
#     NEVER evaluated (thanks to R's lazy argument evaluation), so the slow fit
#     is skipped entirely.
#
# The cache is keyed ONLY on model_id, so once model_cache/<model_id>.rds exists
# the model will never be re-fit. IMPORTANT: if you change a model's formula,
# data, or family, delete its file in model_cache/ (or all of them) so it is
# re-estimated with the new specification.

model_cache_dir <- "model_cache"
if (!dir.exists(model_cache_dir)) dir.create(model_cache_dir)

fit_or_load <- function(model_id, fit_expr) {
  cache_file <- file.path(model_cache_dir, paste0(model_id, ".rds"))

  if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
    message("Loading cached model: ", model_id)
    readRDS(cache_file)            # fit_expr is never touched -> no re-fitting
  } else {
    message("Fitting model (will cache): ", model_id)
    model <- fit_expr             # evaluate the model call now
    saveRDS(model, cache_file)
    model
  }
}

# ---- Regression table renderer ---------------------------------------------
# Renders a fixed-effects table for a (g)lmer model with columns:
#   Predictor | Beta | Std. Error | p | Odds Ratio
# Betas and standard errors are on the log-odds (link) scale; the odds ratio
# column is exp(Beta) and is placed AFTER the p-value column.
render_reg_table <- function(m, title_text, note_text = NULL, pred_labels = NULL) {
  co  <- summary(m)$coefficients
  est <- unname(co[, "Estimate"])
  se  <- unname(co[, "Std. Error"])
  pv  <- unname(co[, ncol(co)])     # final column is the p-value (Pr(>|z|))
  orr <- exp(est)
  terms <- rownames(co)

  labs <- vapply(terms, function(t) {
    if (!is.null(pred_labels) && t %in% names(pred_labels)) pred_labels[[t]] else t
  }, character(1))

  fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))

  df <- data.frame(
    Predictor    = unname(labs),
    Beta         = sprintf("%.3f", est),
    `Std. Error` = sprintf("%.3f", se),
    p            = fmt_p(pv),
    `Odds Ratio` = sprintf("%.3f", orr),
    row.names    = NULL,
    check.names  = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Model-fit information for the footnote
  fit_line <- tryCatch({
    paste0("Observations = ", stats::nobs(m), ". ")
  }, error = function(e) "")
  scale_line <- "Beta and Std. Error are on the log-odds scale; Odds Ratio = exp(Beta)."
  full_note  <- paste0(if (is.null(note_text)) "" else paste0(note_text, " "),
                       fit_line, scale_line)

  # Black + bold caption (HTML)
  caption_html <- paste0("<span style='color:black; font-weight:bold;'>",
                         title_text, "</span>")

  k <- kbl(df, caption = caption_html,
           align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
           booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
           row.names = FALSE) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left",
                  bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
    footnote(general = full_note, general_title = "Note.",
             footnote_as_chunk = TRUE, threeparttable = TRUE)
  print(k)
  cat('<div class="page-break"></div>')
}

```

## Experimental Instructions 

### Study 1 instructions

Participants were presented with the following instructions before they started with the reasoning problems: 
_‘In this experiment, you will see 48 statements about science and technology. We want to understand how strong you think those statements or arguments are. After you read the statement, you will have to click on either “Strong” or “Weak” and then the experiment will automatically advance to the next statement.  We will also ask you how difficult it was for you to make this decision after each statement. Click on “Next” to start the experiment!’_

### Study 2 Instructions

Participants in the *treatment* condition were presented with the following instructions before they started with the reasoning problems: 
_‘In this experiment, you will see 36 statements (in the form of tweets) about science and technology. These statements are accompanied by comments from people who re-shared them - just like you would see on X (formerly Twitter) or other social media such as Facebook. We want to know what you think of these tweets in the light of the accompanying comment._
_This is how the trials will look: [picture of trial]_
_We want to understand how strong you think the original statements or arguments are. You will have to click on either “Weak” or “Strong”. We will also ask you how difficult it was for you to make this decision after each statement. Once you have made up your mind about strength and difficulty, you can click on Next Tweet._
_To ensure that you read both texts, we will first show you the comment for 5 seconds, and then the comment and the questions after that._
_Click on “Next” to start the experiment!’_

Participants in the *control* condition were presented with the following instructions before they started with the reasoning problems: 
_‘In this experiment, you will see 36 statements about science and technology. We want to understand how strong you think those statements or arguments are. After you read the statement, you will have to click on either “Strong” or “Weak” and then the experiment will automatically advance to the next statement.  We will also ask you how difficult it was for you to make this decision after each statement. Click on “Next” to start the experiment!’_

### Study 3 Instructions

Participants in the *treatment* condition were presented with the following instructions before they started with the reasoning problems: 
_‘In this experiment, you will see 36 statements (in the form of tweets) about science and technology. Some of these statements may contain logical fallacies. A fallacy is the use of invalid or otherwise faulty reasoning in the construction of an argument._
_For example, the statement "Aliens must exist because no one has proven they don’t" commits the Appeal to Ignorance fallacy. This is faulty reasoning because a lack of evidence against something does not prove it to be true, just as the inability to disprove unicorns doesn’t mean they exist._
_Some of the statements were checked by an Artificial Intelligence for such argumentative fallacies. When the AI found a fallacy, it created a short warning and a clickable link where the fallacy is explained. If you want to know more, you can click on the link. However, it is not compulsory in this experiment._
_This is how a trial with a fallacy warning will look: [picture of a trial]_
_We want to understand how strong you think the statements or arguments are. We are interested in your true opinion about the statement, NOT the warning. You will have to click on either “Weak” or “Strong”. We will also ask you how difficult it was for you to make this decision after each statement. Once you have made up your mind about strength and difficulty, you can click on Next Tweet._
_Click on “Next” to start the experiment!’_


Participants in the *control* condition were presented with the following instructions before they started with the reasoning problems: 
_‘In this experiment, you will see 36 statements (in the form of tweets) about science and technology. Some of these statements may contain logical fallacies. A fallacy is the use of invalid or otherwise faulty reasoning in the construction of an argument._
_For example, the statement "Aliens must exist because no one has proven they don’t" commits the Appeal to Ignorance fallacy. This is faulty reasoning because a lack of evidence against something does not prove it to be true, just as the inability to disprove unicorns doesn’t mean they exist._
_We want to understand how strong you think the original statements or arguments are. You will have to click on either “Weak” or “Strong”. We will also ask you how difficult it was for you to make this decision after each statement. Once you have made up your mind about strength and difficulty, you can click on Next Tweet._
_Click on “Next” to start the experiment!’_




## Sample composition

```{r sample composition, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}

participant_summary <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    filter(type == "Climate") %>%
    group_by(rid) %>%
    summarise(
      climate_prior = mean(prior, na.rm = TRUE),
      partisanship  = dplyr::first(partisanship_stat),
      climate1_1    = mean(climate1_1, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate2_1    = mean(climate2_1, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_1    = mean(climate3_1, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_2    = mean(climate3_2, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_3    = mean(climate3_3, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_4    = mean(climate3_4, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups       = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # mean() returns NaN when all four climate3_n are NA; convert to NA
      dplyr::across(c(climate1_1, climate2_1, climate3_1, climate3_2,
                      climate3_3, climate3_4),
                    ~ ifelse(is.nan(.x), NA_real_, .x)),
      climate3_avg = rowMeans(
        cbind(climate3_1, climate3_2, climate3_3, climate3_4),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      climate3_avg = ifelse(is.nan(climate3_avg), NA_real_, climate3_avg)
    )
}

# Build a single-row summary for one study (counts + correlations with partisanship)
sample_row <- function(d, study_name) {
  per_pp <- participant_summary(d)
  r_hap <- suppressWarnings(cor(per_pp$climate1_1,   per_pp$partisanship,
                                use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  r_ant <- suppressWarnings(cor(per_pp$climate2_1,   per_pp$partisanship,
                                use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  r_thr <- suppressWarnings(cor(per_pp$climate3_avg, per_pp$partisanship,
                                use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  data.frame(
    Study               = study_name,
    `Total N`           = nrow(per_pp),
    `Climate Skeptics`  = sum(per_pp$climate_prior < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Climate Believers` = sum(per_pp$climate_prior > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    Republicans         = sum(per_pp$partisanship < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    Democrats           = sum(per_pp$partisanship > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    `r(Happening)`      = sprintf("%.2f", r_hap),
    `r(Anthropogenic)`  = sprintf("%.2f", r_ant),
    `r(Threat avg)`     = sprintf("%.2f", r_thr),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

  sample_row(study2_data,  "Study 2a"),

  sample_row(study3_data,  "Study 3")
)
```

## Distribution of prior climate beliefs

The histograms below show, for each study separately, the distribution of participants' raw responses to the three climate prior-belief items. Values are on the original 0–100 scale; the dashed vertical line marks the midpoint at 50. *Note.* The third item ("Climate change is a threat") is computed per participant as the mean of the four sub-items.

```{r prior histograms helper, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

make_prior_hist_row <- function(d, study_name) {

  per_pp <- d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(rid) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      climate1_1 = mean(climate1_1, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate2_1 = mean(climate2_1, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_1 = mean(climate3_1, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_2 = mean(climate3_2, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_3 = mean(climate3_3, na.rm = TRUE),
      climate3_4 = mean(climate3_4, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups    = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(c(climate1_1, climate2_1, climate3_1, climate3_2,
                      climate3_3, climate3_4),
                    ~ifelse(is.nan(.x), NA_real_, .x)),
      climate3_avg = rowMeans(
        cbind(climate3_1, climate3_2, climate3_3, climate3_4),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      climate3_avg = ifelse(is.nan(climate3_avg), NA_real_, climate3_avg)
    )

  hist_one <- function(varname, sub_title) {
    plot_data <- per_pp[!is.na(per_pp[[varname]]), , drop = FALSE]
    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = .data[[varname]])) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed",
                 color = "red", linewidth = 0.7) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = c(0, 50, 100),
        labels = c("More skeptical", "", "More believer"),
        limits = c(-5, 105),                       
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0)
      ) +
      labs(title    = sub_title,
           x        = NULL,
           y        = "N participants") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(plot.title  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11),
            axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
            plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 18, b = 5, l = 8))
  }

  gridExtra::grid.arrange(
    hist_one("climate1_1",   paste0(study_name, ": Climate change is happening")),
    hist_one("climate2_1",   paste0(study_name, ": Climate change is anthropogenic")),
    hist_one("climate3_avg", paste0(study_name, ": Climate change is a threat (avg of 4 items)")),
    ncol = 3
  )
}
```

```{r heterogeneity helpers, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}
pred_labels_het <- c(
  "(Intercept)"                                               = "Intercept",
  "StrengthRecoded"                                           = "Argument Quality",

  "conditiontreatment"                                        = "Treatment (vs. Control)",

render_het_table <- function(m, table_label, subgroup_label) {
  render_reg_table(
    m,
    paste0(table_label, ". Mixed Effects Logistic Regression — ",
           subgroup_label, " (Climate Items)."),
    paste0("Model fit on Climate items in the specified subgroup, with random intercepts ",
           "for participants and arguments. The Republican and Democrat subgroups are ",
           "defined at the participant level. The climate-skeptic and climate-believer ",
           "subgroups are defined at the item level: each argument is classified according ",
           "to the participant's prior belief on the specific climate dimension that ",
           "argument addresses (happening, anthropogenic, or risk). The same participant ",
           "can therefore count as a believer for some items and a skeptic for others - ",
           "for example, believing that climate change is happening (believer) but not ",
           "that it is anthropogenic (skeptic) - and so contributes responses to both ",
           "subgroups."),
    pred_labels_het
  )
}

make_het_barplot <- function(d_sub, plot_title, item_type = "Climate") {

  has_cond <- "condition" %in% names(d_sub) && any(!is.na(d_sub$condition))

  filt <- d_sub %>%
    filter(type == item_type,
           !is.na(Consistency),
           !is.na(strength),
           !is.na(ResponseRecoded))
  if (has_cond) filt <- filt %>% filter(!is.na(condition))

  filt <- filt %>%
    mutate(
      Consistency = factor(Consistency, levels = c("Consistent", "Inconsistent")),
      strength    = factor(strength,    levels = c("Strong", "Weak"),
                           labels = c("Strong (valid)", "Weak (fallacious)"))
    )
  if (has_cond) {
    filt <- filt %>%
      mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("control", "treatment"),
                                labels = c("Control", "Treatment")))
    summary_data <- filt %>%
      group_by(strength, Consistency, condition)
  } else {
    summary_data <- filt %>%
      group_by(strength, Consistency)
  }

  summary_data <- summary_data %>%
    summarise(
      mean_resp = mean(ResponseRecoded, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      se        = sd(ResponseRecoded, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()) * 100,
      .groups   = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = pmax(mean_resp - 1.96 * se, 0),
      ci_upper = pmin(mean_resp + 1.96 * se, 100)
    )

  # One value per participant per cell, for the overlaid dots. A fixed jitter
  # seed keeps the displayed figure and the saved PDF pixel-identical.
  if (has_cond) {
    pp_data <- filt %>%
      group_by(rid, strength, Consistency, condition)
  } else {
    pp_data <- filt %>%
      group_by(rid, strength, Consistency)
  }
  pp_data <- pp_data %>%
    summarise(pp_mean = mean(ResponseRecoded, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
              .groups = "drop")

  # Panel subtitle: number of unique participants contributing to this panel,
  # split by condition where a condition exists (Study 1 has none).
  if (has_cond) {
    n_ctrl <- dplyr::n_distinct(filt$rid[filt$condition == "Control"])
    n_trt  <- dplyr::n_distinct(filt$rid[filt$condition == "Treatment"])
    sub_txt <- sprintf("Control N = %d, Treatment N = %d", n_ctrl, n_trt)
  } else {
    sub_txt <- sprintf("N = %d", dplyr::n_distinct(filt$rid))
  }

  if (has_cond) {
    p <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = Consistency, y = mean_resp,
                                  fill = condition, color = condition)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(0.9),
               width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
      geom_point(data = pp_data,
                 aes(x = Consistency, y = pp_mean, group = condition),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.32,
                                                 jitter.height = 2.5,
                                                 dodge.width = 0.9,
                                                 seed = 42),
                 shape = 16, size = 0.6, alpha = 0.25, colour = "grey15") +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                    position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.2,
                    color = "black") +
      labs(fill = "Condition", color = "Condition")
  } else {
    p <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = Consistency, y = mean_resp,
                                  fill = Consistency)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
      geom_point(data = pp_data,
                 aes(x = Consistency, y = pp_mean),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 position = position_jitter(width = 0.26, height = 2.5, seed = 42),
                 shape = 16, size = 0.6, alpha = 0.25, colour = "grey15") +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                    width = 0.2, color = "black") +
      guides(fill = "none")
  }

  p +
    facet_wrap(~ strength) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
    # slightly wider than 0-100 so vertically jittered points at the floor and
    # ceiling are not clipped; axis ticks still run 0-100
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-4, 104)) +
    labs(
      title    = plot_title,
      subtitle = sub_txt,
      x        = "Consistency to prior belief",
      y        = "Perceived strength(%)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
}

# Save a figure (a ggplot or a grid/gridExtra grob) to figures/ as a
# publication-quality PDF. PDF output is vector, hence resolution-independent;
# dpi = 300 is passed so that any raster component is rendered at 300 dpi.
# cairo_pdf is preferred because the panel titles contain UTF-8 em dashes.
save_fig_pdf <- function(plot_obj, filename, width, height, dpi = 300) {
  if (!dir.exists("figures")) dir.create("figures", recursive = TRUE)
  dev_fun <- if (isTRUE(capabilities("cairo"))) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = file.path("figures", filename),
    plot     = plot_obj,
    width    = width, height = height, units = "in",
    dpi      = dpi, device = dev_fun
  )
  invisible(file.path("figures", filename))
}

```

*Note.* The figures above show strength perception (mean percentage of Climate arguments judged "Strong") in Study 1, plotted by consistency to prior belief (x-axis) and argument quality (facets), separately for Democrats, Republicans, climate skeptics, and climate believers. The Democrat and Republican panels are defined at the participant level, but the climate-skeptic and climate-believer panels are defined at the *item* level: each argument is classified according to the participant's prior belief on the specific climate dimension that argument addresses (whether climate change is happening, whether it is anthropogenic, or whether it poses a risk). The same participant can therefore count as a believer for some items and a skeptic for others — for example, believing that climate change is happening (believer) but not that it is anthropogenic (skeptic) — and so contributes responses to both panels. Their Ns consequently do not sum to the total sample. Overlaid points are individual participants' mean responses within each cell (jittered horizontally, and slightly vertically, to reduce overplotting). Error bars are 95% confidence intervals. Sample size: *N* = 1195.

## Study 2a and 2b effect heterogeneity over partisanship and prior beliefs

We conducted several exploratory analyses to test whether the treatment effects were the same across prior beliefs (climate skeptics vs. climate believers), partisanship (Republicans vs. Democrats) and fallacy types. Note that the skeptic/believer split is defined at the item level rather than the participant level: each argument is classified according to the participant's prior belief on the specific climate dimension that argument addresses (happening, anthropogenic, or risk), so the same participant can count as a believer for some items and a skeptic for others — for example, believing that climate change is happening (believer) but not that it is anthropogenic (skeptic). The treatment's effect on evaluation was broadly consistent across these subgroups. Because prior-consistent arguments are anti-climate for skeptics but pro-climate for believers, the common shift away from prior-consistent positions appears as a treatment × argument direction interaction of opposite sign in the two groups; in both, it reflects downgrading of the prior-consistent arguments in Study 2a (skeptics $b = 0.74$, believers $b = -0.42$, both $p < .001$) and the corresponding shift in Study 2b (believers $b = -0.38, p < .001$; weaker and non-significant among skeptics, $b = -0.16, p = .341$). The effect held similarly across the political spectrum, reaching significance for both Republicans (Study 2a: $b = -0.35$; Study 2b: $b = -0.31$, both $p < .001$) and Democrats (Study 2a: $b = -0.30, p < .001$; Study 2b: $b = -0.23, p = .008$). Across fallacy types, we observe the same patterns as in the aggregate results (see Tables S32 and S33): perceived strength of strong arguments and of each individual fallacy type moved uniformly under treatment, downward in Study 2a, where the retweets contested the target argument, and upward in Study 2b, where the retweets endorsed the target argument.

### Simple effects: treatment effect within each (partisan identity × argument direction) cell (Studies 2a and 2b)

```{r simple effects treatment within partisan x direction cells, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}


fit_tx_cell <- function(d, model_id) {
  tryCatch({
    m <- fit_or_load(model_id, lme4::glmer(
      ResponseRecoded ~ condition + (1 | rid) + (1 | unique_id),
      data   = d,
      family = binomial(),
      na.action = na.omit
    ))
    co <- summary(m)$coefficients
    if ("conditiontreatment" %in% rownames(co)) {
      list(b  = co["conditiontreatment", "Estimate"],
           se = co["conditiontreatment", "Std. Error"],
           p  = co["conditiontreatment", ncol(co)])
    } else {
      list(b = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
    }
  }, error = function(e) list(b = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
}

fmt_p_cell <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "—",
                                 ifelse(p < .001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))

cell_row <- function(d_full, partisan_filter, direction_value, label, model_id) {
  d <- d_full %>%
    dplyr::filter(type == "Climate",
                  !is.na(partisanship_stat), !is.na(direction),
                  !is.na(condition), !is.na(ResponseRecoded),
                  partisan_filter(partisanship_stat),
                  direction == direction_value)

  ctrl_mean <- mean(d$ResponseRecoded[d$condition == "control"],   na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  tx_mean   <- mean(d$ResponseRecoded[d$condition == "treatment"], na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  diff_pp   <- tx_mean - ctrl_mean
  res       <- fit_tx_cell(d, model_id)

  data.frame(
    Subgroup   = label,
    Control    = sprintf("%.1f", ctrl_mean),
    Treatment  = sprintf("%.1f", tx_mean),
    Difference = sprintf("%+.1f", diff_pp),
    Beta       = ifelse(is.na(res$b),  "—", sprintf("%+.3f", res$b)),
    SE         = ifelse(is.na(res$se), "—", sprintf("%.3f",  res$se)),
    p          = fmt_p_cell(res$p),
    OR         = ifelse(is.na(res$b),  "—", sprintf("%.3f",  exp(res$b))),
    N          = length(unique(d$rid)),
    row.names  = NULL, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

is_rep <- function(x) x < 0
is_dem <- function(x) x > 0

cells_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  # Study 2a — 4 cells
  cell_row(study2_data,  is_rep, "Contra/Nonrisky", "Republicans × Contra/Non-risky", "model_tx_2a_rep_contra"),
  cell_row(study2_data,  is_rep, "Pro/Risky",       "Republicans × Pro/Risky",       "model_tx_2a_rep_pro"),
  cell_row(study2_data,  is_dem, "Contra/Nonrisky", "Democrats × Contra/Non-risky",   "model_tx_2a_dem_contra"),
  cell_row(study2_data,  is_dem, "Pro/Risky",       "Democrats × Pro/Risky",          "model_tx_2a_dem_pro"),
  # Study 2b — 4 cells
  cell_row(study2b_data, is_rep, "Contra/Nonrisky", "Republicans × Contra/Non-risky", "model_tx_2b_rep_contra"),
  cell_row(study2b_data, is_rep, "Pro/Risky",       "Republicans × Pro/Risky",       "model_tx_2b_rep_pro"),
  cell_row(study2b_data, is_dem, "Contra/Nonrisky", "Democrats × Contra/Non-risky",   "model_tx_2b_dem_contra"),
  cell_row(study2b_data, is_dem, "Pro/Risky",       "Democrats × Pro/Risky",          "model_tx_2b_dem_pro")
)

kbl(
  cells_tbl,
  caption  = paste0("<span style='color:black; font-weight:bold;'>",
                    "Table S26. Simple effects: Treatment vs. Control within each ",
                    "(partisan identity × argument direction) cell, Studies 2a and 2b ",
                    "(Climate items).</span>"),
  col.names = c("Subgroup",
                "Control", "Treatment", "Difference (Tx − Ctrl)",
                "Beta", "SE", "p", "Odds Ratio", "N participants"),
  align    = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
  booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left",
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1,
                     "Mean % 'Strong' judgments" = 3,
                     "Mixed-effects logistic regression" = 4,
                     " " = 1)) %>%
  pack_rows("Study 2a", 1, 4, bold = TRUE) %>%
  pack_rows("Study 2b", 5, 8, bold = TRUE) %>%
  footnote(
    general = paste0(
      "Each row decomposes a single (partisan identity × argument direction) cell ",
      "of the Climate items. The 'Control' and 'Treatment' columns are the raw mean ",
      "percentage of arguments judged 'Strong' within that cell; 'Difference ",
      "(Tx − Ctrl)' is their raw difference in percentage points. ",
      "Beta is the conditiontreatment main effect from a cell-specific mixed-effects ",
      "logistic regression: ResponseRecoded ~ condition + (1|rid) + (1|unique_id), ",
      "binomial logit. SE and p are clustering-adjusted via the random intercepts ",
      "for participants and items."
    ),
    general_title    = "Note.",
    footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
    threeparttable   = TRUE
  ) %>%
  print()

cat('<div class="page-break"></div>')
```

### Study 3 — treatment effect by demographic subgroup (Climate items)

```{r study 3 demographic heterogeneity, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}


pick_best_col <- function(d, candidates) {
  candidates <- intersect(candidates, names(d))
  if (length(candidates) == 0) return(NULL)
  best  <- candidates[1]
  best_n <- -1L
  for (cn in candidates) {
    nn <- d %>% dplyr::distinct(rid, .data[[cn]]) %>%
      dplyr::pull(.data[[cn]])
    n  <- sum(!is.na(nn) & nn != "" & nn != " ")
    if (n > best_n) { best <- cn; best_n <- n }
  }
  best
}

gender_col <- pick_best_col(study3_data, c("Gender", "gender", "Gender.1", "gender.1"))
age_col    <- pick_best_col(study3_data, c("age", "age.1", "Age"))
edu_col    <- pick_best_col(study3_data, c("education", "education.1", "Education"))

demo_pp <- study3_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "Climate") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(rid) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Gender_raw = dplyr::first(.data[[gender_col]]),
    age_raw    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(dplyr::first(.data[[age_col]]))),
    edu_raw    = dplyr::first(.data[[edu_col]]),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )


age_median <- stats::median(demo_pp$age_raw, na.rm = TRUE)

is_college_plus <- function(x) {
  num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  txt <- toupper(as.character(x))
  num_ge5 <- !is.na(num) & num >= 5
  txt_hit <- grepl("BACHELOR|MASTER|DOCTOR|PROFESSIONAL|PHD|MBA|\\bMD\\b|\\bJD\\b|GRADUATE\\s+DEGREE",
                   txt)
  num_ge5 | txt_hit
}

demo_pp <- demo_pp %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Gender_grp = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("^F", Gender_raw, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Female",
      grepl("^M", Gender_raw, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Male",
      TRUE                                        ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Age_grp = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(age_raw)         ~ NA_character_,
      age_raw <  age_median  ~ paste0("Younger (< ", age_median, ")"),
      age_raw >= age_median  ~ paste0("Older (≥ ", age_median, ")"),
      TRUE                   ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Edu_grp = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(edu_raw) | edu_raw == "" ~ NA_character_,
      is_college_plus(edu_raw)       ~ "College or higher (Bachelor's+)",
      TRUE                           ~ "Lower than college (no Bachelor's)"
    )
  )

strong_long <- study3_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "Climate",
                !is.na(condition), !is.na(strength),
                !is.na(ResponseRecoded)) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(demo_pp %>% dplyr::select(rid, Gender_grp, Age_grp, Edu_grp),
                    by = "rid")

fit_qxt_interaction <- function(d, model_id) {
  tryCatch({
    # Cached via fit_or_load so each demographic subgroup only re-fits when its
    # cache file is missing.
    m <- fit_or_load(model_id, lme4::glmer(
      ResponseRecoded ~ StrengthRecoded * condition + (1 | rid) + (1 | unique_id),
      data   = d,
      family = binomial(),
      na.action = na.omit
    ))
    co <- summary(m)$coefficients
    if ("StrengthRecoded:conditiontreatment" %in% rownames(co)) {
      list(b = co["StrengthRecoded:conditiontreatment", "Estimate"],
           p = co["StrengthRecoded:conditiontreatment", ncol(co)])
    } else {
      list(b = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
    }
  }, error = function(e) list(b = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
}

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "—",
                            ifelse(p < .001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))

subgroup_row <- function(d, subgroup_label, model_id) {
  s <- d %>%
    dplyr::mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("control", "treatment")),
                  strength  = factor(strength,  levels = c("Strong", "Weak"))) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(strength, condition) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(m = mean(ResponseRecoded, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop")

  pull <- function(str_lvl, cond_lvl) {
    v <- s$m[s$strength == str_lvl & s$condition == cond_lvl]
    if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v)) NA_real_ else v
  }
  s_ctrl <- pull("Strong", "control");    s_tx <- pull("Strong", "treatment")
  w_ctrl <- pull("Weak",   "control");    w_tx <- pull("Weak",   "treatment")
  n_pp   <- length(unique(d$rid))

  mi <- fit_qxt_interaction(d, model_id)

  data.frame(
    Subgroup     = subgroup_label,
    N            = n_pp,
    Strong_ctrl  = sprintf("%.1f", s_ctrl),
    Strong_tx    = sprintf("%.1f", s_tx),
    Strong_diff  = sprintf("%+.1f", s_tx - s_ctrl),
    Weak_ctrl    = sprintf("%.1f", w_ctrl),
    Weak_tx      = sprintf("%.1f", w_tx),
    Weak_diff    = sprintf("%+.1f", w_tx - w_ctrl),
    Int_b        = ifelse(is.na(mi$b), "—", sprintf("%+.3f", mi$b)),
    Int_p        = fmt_p(mi$p),
    row.names    = NULL, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

rows <- list()


for (g in c("Female", "Male")) {
  d <- strong_long %>% dplyr::filter(Gender_grp == g)
  if (nrow(d) > 0)
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- subgroup_row(d, g,
                                             paste0("model_s3_demo_gender_", tolower(g)))
}
# Age (Younger first, Older second)
for (lvl in sort(unique(stats::na.omit(strong_long$Age_grp)))) {
  d <- strong_long %>% dplyr::filter(Age_grp == lvl)
  if (nrow(d) > 0) {
    age_tag <- if (grepl("Younger", lvl)) "younger" else "older"
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- subgroup_row(d, lvl,
                                             paste0("model_s3_demo_age_", age_tag))
  }
}
for (e in c("College or higher (Bachelor's+)", "Lower than college (no Bachelor's)")) {
  d <- strong_long %>% dplyr::filter(Edu_grp == e)
  if (nrow(d) > 0) {
    edu_tag <- if (grepl("College or higher", e)) "collegeplus" else "subcollege"
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- subgroup_row(d, e,
                                             paste0("model_s3_demo_edu_", edu_tag))
  }
}

demo_tbl <- do.call(rbind, rows)

kbl(
  demo_tbl,
  caption  = paste0("<span style='color:black; font-weight:bold;'>",
                    "Table S31. Study 3 — average treatment effect on judging arguments as ",
                    "'Strong' (Climate items), broken out by demographic subgroup.</span>"),
  col.names = c("Subgroup", "N",
                "Control", "Treatment", "Difference",
                "Control", "Treatment", "Difference",
                "β", "p"),
  align    = c("l", "r", rep("r", 8)),
  booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left",
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2,
                     "Strong arguments (% 'Strong')" = 3,
                     "Weak arguments (% 'Strong')" = 3,
                     "Argument Quality × Treatment" = 2)) %>%
  pack_rows("Gender",    1, 2, bold = TRUE) %>%
  pack_rows("Age (median split)",  3, 4, bold = TRUE) %>%
  pack_rows("Education", 5, 6, bold = TRUE) %>%
  footnote(
    general = paste0(
      "Cells in the 'Control' and 'Treatment' columns are the raw % of arguments ",
      "judged 'Strong' within that subgroup. 'Difference' is Treatment - Control ",
      "in percentage points (a negative value on the Weak side means the logical-",
      "warning treatment lowered the rate at which weak arguments were judged 'Strong', ",
      "which is Study 3's expected pattern). N is the number of unique participants. ",
      "The 'Argument Quality × Treatment' columns report the within-subgroup ",
      "interaction coefficient (Beta) and p-value from a mixed-effects logistic ",
      "regression ResponseRecoded ~ StrengthRecoded * condition + (1|rid) + ",
      "(1|unique_id), fit on the Climate items in that subgroup. A positive, ",
      "significant Beta means the treatment widened the gap between Strong and ",
      "Weak arguments within that subgroup (i.e., improved discrimination), which ",
      "is Study 3's predicted pattern. Subgroup definitions: Gender = self-reported ",
      "Female / Male (other / missing excluded). Age = median split on the numeric ",
      "age variable. Education = 'College or higher' means the participant reported ",
      "at least a 4-year Bachelor's degree (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctoral, or ",
      "Professional degree); 'Lower than college' covers less than high school, ",
      "high-school graduate, some college without a degree, and Associate's (2-year) ",
      "degree."
    ),
    general_title    = "Note.",
    footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
    threeparttable   = TRUE
  ) %>%
  print()

cat('<div class="page-break"></div>')

```


## Average perceived strength per fallacy type and per condition

```{r Study 1-3 fallacy means by condition, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='asis'}

args_json <- fromJSON("arguments_augmented.json")
arg_type_lookup <- args_json %>%
  select(argumentNumber, type) %>%
  rename(unique_id = argumentNumber, arg_type = type)

# Row order: Strong + the 4 weak-argument fallacy types
fallacy_levels <- c(
  "Strong",
  "Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc",
  "Overgeneralization",
  "Affirming the Consequent",
  "Denying the Antecedent"
)

add_fallacy_cat <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    left_join(arg_type_lookup, by = "unique_id") %>%
    mutate(
      fallacy_cat = case_when(
        strength == "Strong"                    ~ "Strong",
        arg_type == "post hoc ergo propter hoc" ~ "Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc",
        arg_type == "overgeneralization"        ~ "Overgeneralization",
        arg_type == "affirming the consequent"  ~ "Affirming the Consequent",
        arg_type == "denying the antecedent"    ~ "Denying the Antecedent",
        TRUE                                    ~ NA_character_
      ),
      fallacy_cat = factor(fallacy_cat, levels = fallacy_levels)
    )
}

summarise_row <- function(d, item_type, row_label, cond_filter = NULL) {
  out <- d %>%
    filter(type == item_type, !is.na(fallacy_cat), !is.na(ResponseRecoded))
  if (!is.null(cond_filter)) {
    out <- out %>% filter(condition == cond_filter)
  }
  out %>%
    group_by(fallacy_cat) %>%
    summarise(
      cell = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)",
                     mean(ResponseRecoded, na.rm = TRUE),
                     sd(ResponseRecoded, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = fallacy_cat, values_from = cell) %>%
    mutate(Condition = row_label, .before = 1)
}

s1_fc  <- add_fallacy_cat(study1_data)
s2_fc  <- add_fallacy_cat(study2_data)
s2b_fc <- add_fallacy_cat(study2b_data)
s3_fc  <- add_fallacy_cat(study3_data)

make_combined_table <- function(item_type, table_label, caption_text) {

  rows <- bind_rows(
    summarise_row(s1_fc,  item_type, "Overall"),                              # Study 1: no condition
    summarise_row(s2_fc,  item_type, "Control",   cond_filter = "control"),
    summarise_row(s2_fc,  item_type, "Treatment", cond_filter = "treatment"),
    summarise_row(s2b_fc, item_type, "Control",   cond_filter = "control"),
    summarise_row(s2b_fc, item_type, "Treatment", cond_filter = "treatment"),
    summarise_row(s3_fc,  item_type, "Control",   cond_filter = "control"),
    summarise_row(s3_fc,  item_type, "Treatment", cond_filter = "treatment")
  )

  for (lvl in fallacy_levels) {
    if (!lvl %in% names(rows)) rows[[lvl]] <- NA_character_
  }
  rows <- rows[, c("Condition", fallacy_levels)]

  # Replace NA cells (empty groups) with em-dash
  rows[] <- lapply(rows, function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", as.character(x)))

  # Shorter column headers for the (narrow) fallacy columns
  display_names <- c(
    "Strong",
    "Post Hoc",
    "Overgeneralization",
    "Affirming the Consequent",
    "Denying the Antecedent"
  )

  kbl(
    rows,
    caption  = paste0("<span style='color:black; font-weight:bold;'>",
                      table_label, ". ", caption_text, "</span>"),
    align    = c("l", rep("c", length(fallacy_levels))),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape   = FALSE,
    col.names = c("", display_names)
  ) %>%
    kable_styling(
      full_width        = FALSE,
      position          = "left",
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      latex_options     = c("hold_position", "scale_down")
    ) %>%
    add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Argument Type" = length(fallacy_levels))) %>%
    pack_rows("Study 1",  1, 1, bold = TRUE, italic = FALSE) %>%
    pack_rows("Study 2a", 2, 3, bold = TRUE, italic = FALSE) %>%
    pack_rows("Study 2b", 4, 5, bold = TRUE, italic = FALSE) %>%
    pack_rows("Study 3",  6, 7, bold = TRUE, italic = FALSE) %>%
    footnote(
      general = paste0(
        "Cells show M (SD) of ResponseRecoded (1 = judged Strong, 0 = judged Weak). ",
        "The 'Strong' column pools all ", tolower(item_type),
        " arguments without an argumentative fallacy; the four fallacy columns are weak ",
        tolower(item_type), " arguments classified by error type. ",
        "Study 1 had no treatment manipulation; Studies 2a, 2b, and 3 are split by ",
        "experimental condition (Control vs. Treatment)."
      ),
      general_title    = "Note.",
      footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
      threeparttable   = TRUE
    ) %>%
    print()

  cat('<div class="page-break"></div>')
}

    "Climate Arguments by Study, Condition, and Argument Type."
  )
)

fit_tx_fallacy <- function(d, model_id) {
  tryCatch({
    m <- fit_or_load(model_id, lme4::glmer(
      ResponseRecoded ~ condition + (1 | rid) + (1 | unique_id),
      data   = d,
      family = binomial(),
      na.action = na.omit
    ))
    co <- summary(m)$coefficients
    if ("conditiontreatment" %in% rownames(co)) {
      list(b  = co["conditiontreatment", "Estimate"],
           se = co["conditiontreatment", "Std. Error"],
           p  = co["conditiontreatment", ncol(co)])
    } else {
      list(b = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
    }
  }, error = function(e) list(b = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
}

fmt_p_fal <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "—",
                                ifelse(p < .001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))

fallacy_label_to_tag <- c(
  "Strong"                     = "strong",
  "Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc"  = "posthoc",
  "Overgeneralization"         = "overgen",
  "Affirming the Consequent"   = "affirm",
  "Denying the Antecedent"     = "denying"
)

fallacy_tx_row <- function(d_aug, item_type, fallacy_level, study_tag, item_tag) {
  d_cell <- d_aug %>%
    dplyr::filter(type == item_type,
                  fallacy_cat == fallacy_level,
                  !is.na(condition),
                  !is.na(ResponseRecoded))

  n_pp <- length(unique(d_cell$rid))

  if (nrow(d_cell) == 0 ||
      length(unique(d_cell$condition[d_cell$condition %in% c("control", "treatment")])) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(
      Subgroup = as.character(fallacy_level),
      Beta = "—", SE = "—", p = "—", OR = "—",
      row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }

  fal_tag  <- fallacy_label_to_tag[[as.character(fallacy_level)]]
  model_id <- paste0("model_fx_", study_tag, "_", item_tag, "_", fal_tag)
  res      <- fit_tx_fallacy(d_cell, model_id)

  data.frame(
    Subgroup = as.character(fallacy_level),
    Beta     = ifelse(is.na(res$b),  "—", sprintf("%+.3f", res$b)),
    SE       = ifelse(is.na(res$se), "—", sprintf("%.3f",  res$se)),
    p        = fmt_p_fal(res$p),
    OR       = ifelse(is.na(res$b),  "—", sprintf("%.3f",  exp(res$b))),
    row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

build_fallacy_analyses_table <- function(item_type, item_tag, table_label, item_label) {

  rows <- list()
  for (lvl in fallacy_levels) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- fallacy_tx_row(s2_fc,  item_type, lvl, "2a", item_tag)
  for (lvl in fallacy_levels) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- fallacy_tx_row(s2b_fc, item_type, lvl, "2b", item_tag)
  for (lvl in fallacy_levels) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- fallacy_tx_row(s3_fc,  item_type, lvl, "s3", item_tag)
  analyses_tbl <- do.call(rbind, rows)

  kbl(
    analyses_tbl,
    caption  = paste0("<span style='color:black; font-weight:bold;'>",
                      table_label, ". Treatment vs. Control simple-effects analyses ",
                      "for each argument type within each study, ",
                      item_label, " items.</span>"),
    col.names = c("Argument Type", "Beta", "SE", "p", "Odds Ratio"),
    align    = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE
  ) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left",
                  bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
    pack_rows("Study 2a", 1, length(fallacy_levels),                              bold = TRUE) %>%
    pack_rows("Study 2b", length(fallacy_levels) + 1, 2 * length(fallacy_levels), bold = TRUE) %>%
    pack_rows("Study 3",  2 * length(fallacy_levels) + 1, 3 * length(fallacy_levels), bold = TRUE) %>%
    footnote(
      general = paste0(
        "Each row reports the conditiontreatment main effect from a cell-specific ",
        "mixed-effects logistic regression: ResponseRecoded ~ condition + (1|rid) + ",
        "(1|unique_id), binomial logit, restricted to ", item_label, " items. ",
        "The 'Strong' row pools all ", tolower(item_label),
        " arguments that are not classified as fallacious; the four fallacy rows ",
        "use the argument-type classification from arguments_augmented.json. ",
        "Study 1 is omitted because it has no treatment manipulation."
      ),
      general_title    = "Note.",
      footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
      threeparttable   = TRUE
    ) %>%
    print()

  cat('<div class="page-break"></div>')
}

build_fallacy_analyses_table("Climate", "climate", "Table S34", "Climate")
build_fallacy_analyses_table("Neutral", "neutral", "Table S35", "Neutral")
```
